The Aquarium

Warm water, six metres of it. Drag to look around, scroll to move through the tank, click the glass to drop a pinch of food and watch them come.

the light on the sand

The net of light down there is not a texture. Every frame a quarter of a million sun rays are bent through the real rippled surface and splatted where they land — the bright cords are simply where a lot of them piled up.

Show the fold draws a second, separate calculation on top: the curve where det(I + a·H) = 0, out of the surface's own curvature, with no rays in it whatsoever. It lands on the cords — because a caustic is exactly where a bundle of rays folds through itself.

Chop is the height of the ripples. Wind the sun down and the cords fade into a soft mottle; wind clarity down and the far glass disappears into green — red goes first, which is the whole reason water looks like water.

the air

A bubble is a spring — the gas inside is the spring, the water round it the mass — so its note is set by nothing but its size: f₀ · r ≈ 3.29 Hz·m. Every bubble you see is voiced at the pitch its own drawn radius demands, which is why the fat lazy ones go bloop and the fine ones hiss.

This room needs WebGL2. It renders a live reef — the light on the sand is a quarter of a million refracted rays, splatted every frame — and there is no honest way to fake that without a GPU. Any current desktop browser will show it.
